properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/05/2026 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Jefferson Township, Fayette county. 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/05/2026
Violation Code: 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
Violation ID: 8267022
Permit API: 051-22256
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Jefferson Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/05/2026
Comments: On March 5, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 4151444.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. Stage of plugging operations was not confirmed during this inspection.RCE is not installed as depicted on the E and S plan. Surface/vegetation disturbance beyond the width of the access road remains near the entrance as observed in IR 4151444. Plastic matting on access road remains in the same two areas (Photos 7-10).CFS is observed along the access road only on either side of the road at the pre-existing culvert (Photos 11-16). Both sections of CFS are not installed properly as stakes are missing and/or are separated by 10 or more feet between stakes. The CFS on the culvert's outlet side is currently overtopping and causing an erosion channel to begin to form downslope of the CFS. Sediment is not observed to be discharging into the Waters of the Commonwealth at this time.Production tank is observed contained within an adequately vegetated earthen berm. No spills, leaks, or releases are observed at the production tank at this time. Pooling of stormwater is observed along the access road closer to the site (Photos 22-23). This water is observed to be exiting the access road and causing an erosion channel to begin to form downslope. No CFS is observed at this area.CFS is observed to be present along the downslope side of the well site as depicted in the E and S plan, however it is not properly installed as stakes are missing and/or are separated by 10 or more feet between stakes (Photos 24-25). Water is currently pooling along the CFS at an area where the stakes have been removed from the surface.The Department recommends the operator install controls in accordance with the construction sequence and the E and S plan.The Department recommends the operator maintain all BMPs on-site and install additional controls where necessary, as per the E and S plan.The Department recommends the operator seed and mulch or otherwise temporarily stabilize the affected areas of erosion.Violations are continued for failing to construct the site in accordance with the E and S plan and for improperly installed CFS.New violations are being issued for erosion and sedimentation and additional sections of improperly installed CFS.

Violation ID: 8286892
Permit API: 051-22973
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Washington Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/28/2026
Comments: On 8/28/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection of the Orr 14 OG well in Washington Township, Fayette County.The inspection was conducted in response to a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug the well, received on 8/25/2026.At the time of inspection, the following was observed:- The access road appears to be a multi-use road that is shared with additional Diversified well sites. Evidence of minor stormwater washout was observed in portions of the shared access road at the time of inspection. The well site is located within a forested agricultural area. Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is installed downslope of the well site. The area surrounding the well site is heavily saturated, with evidence of heavy animal traffic observable at the time of inspection. The E and S/Restoration plan was not located on site during this inspection. However, the E and S/Restoration plan was located during a Department SubSurface inspection (IR 4266229) that overlaps the time of this inspection.- The gas well is equipped with a well tag. No additional equipment related to well plugging and/or production was observed on site during this inspection. The Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) was not observed on site.- While on site, the Department spoke with Ed from Glade Pipeline Services, who confirmed that third-party disturbances are occurring at the well site due to livestock grazing, and explained that they were on site to make repairs on the access road and the well site.- Upon exiting the site toward Connellsville Street, the Department observed loose soil that had been pushed adjacent to an apparent unnamed tributary to Downers Run during today's aforementioned access road repairs (Photos 17-20). Although no sediment was observed entering this apparent unnamed tributary to Downers Run at the time of inspection, it is actively under threat by this site since no E and S control measures are installed in this location. The Department recommends that the operator take immediate action to cease ongoing threats to the Waters of the Commonwealth.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure implement adequate Erosion and Sedimentation control measures prior to conducting earth disturbances on the access road, which is resulting in a threat to the Waters of the Commonwealth. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending review of the site E and S plan in a subsequent surface inspection.An additional violation will be issued in IR 4265922 for failure to post the Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) on site.While on site, the Department notified Diversified representative Daniel Frick via voicemail of the Department's observations and forthcoming violations from this inspection and IR 4265922.

Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is installed downslope of the well site. The area surrounding the well site is heavily saturated, with evidence of heavy animal traffic observable at the time of inspection. The E and S/Restoration plan was not located on site during this inspection. However, the E and S/Restoration plan was located during a Department SubSurface inspection (IR 4266229) that overlaps the time of this inspection.- The gas well is equipped with a well tag. No additional equipment related to well plugging and/or production was observed on site during this inspection. The Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) was not observed on site.- While on site, the Department spoke with Ed from Glade Pipeline Services, who confirmed that third-party disturbances are occurring at the well site due to livestock grazing, and explained that they were on site to make repairs on the access road and the well site.- Upon exiting the site toward Connellsville Street, the Department observed loose soil that had been pushed adjacent to an apparent unnamed tributary to Downers Run during today's aforementioned access road repairs (Photos 17-20). Although no sediment was observed entering this apparent unnamed tributary to Downers Run at the time of inspection, it is actively under threat by this site since no E and S control measures are installed in this location. The Department recommends that the operator take immediate action to cease ongoing threats to the Waters of the Commonwealth.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure implement adequate Erosion and Sedimentation control measures prior to conducting earth disturbances on the access road, which is resulting in a threat to the Waters of the Commonwealth. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending review of the site E and S plan in a subsequent surface inspection.An additional violation will be issued in IR 4265922 for failure to post the Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) on site.While on site, the Department notified Diversified representative Daniel Frick via voicemail of the Department's observations and forthcoming violations from this inspection and IR 4265922.

Comments: On August 7, 2025, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Burnett Oil Co Inc's Stickle Ross Mountain Unit 1H well (129-28648) located in Fairfield Township, Westmoreland County following IR 4011505, where the Department observed several areas of the graveled well pad to have an oily substance on it, specifically in areas relating to the reported re-plugging of the 129-28648 well. Accompanying during today's inspection is Monona Operator/Land Owner Tom Stickle and Plants and Goodwin's Representative Jim Watson.Burnett Oil representative Walter Glasgow stated in an email to the Department (documented in IR 4029448), that clean up began on 7/28/25 and was completed on 7/31/25, once the Department conducts an inspection of the site to determine if all contaminated material was removed, Burnett will replace the removed rock from the graveled well site. Once Waste Management disposes of the contaminated material, Burnett Oil will provide the Department with a quantity of the release. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed an Act 9 sign at the access road entrance to not be in compliance and inside the on-site mailbox was an outdated Emergency Response Plan (ERP). Violations associated with the Act 9 Sign and the ERP are addressed under a separate inspection for 129-28411. An access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel and the perimeters of the well site were observed to be exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative cover with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed.At the time of this inspection, the 1H: 129-28648 well appeared to be plugged and all plugging equipment appeared to be removed from the well site. A new monument and vent pipe which was reportedly approved by the Department was observed to be installed. The monument was observed to have the plugged well's permit number and replug date posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this plugged well.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the graveled well pad to be scraped in the areas that were previously observed to have an oily substance during IR 4013514. At the time of this inspection, the Department did not observe an oily or shiny brown substance anywhere on the graveled well pad. Mr. Watson stated that all contaminated material was placed in the roll off dumpster observed on site, that new gravel will be laid in the release areas and the contaminated material will be properly disposed of following this inspection. The Department requested a waste manifest for the disposed contaminated material be provided to the Department upon its receipt to verify whether the release was less than 42 gallons, and therefore remediated applicably under 78a.66(c)(1). If the quantity of the release is over 42 gallons, the Department recommends the Operator follow the Act 2 guidelines for remediation as set by 78a.66(c)(2).Based on today's inspection, violations issued for an oily substance on the graveled well pad shall remain outstanding at this time pending the receipt of a waste manifest and a quantity of the release.

Replacement of topsoil and vegetation of this area needs to be coordinated with landowner and State Forest representatives. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-08-28 to Swn Prod Co Llc in Liberty Twp, Tioga county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 860201
Permit API: 117-22055
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Liberty Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-08-28
Comments: I inspected the site in response to a reported spill(Complaint ID#344679). I met Mike Deming of SWN when I arrived. He informed me that after washing and vaccing the liner yesterday, the liner and felt were placed in 4 rolloff containers that Waste Management had sent to the site without interior liners. In the process of loading the liner and felt into the containers, the loader compresses the material with the bucket; soapy water was then observed running out of the end of the rolloffs. Mike believes that the felt retained some rig wash solution (SDS forthcoming) and water, and that the compression of the material squeezed this mix out. He stated that the estimate of 2 barrels (84 gallons) was probably high, but that SWN was committed to an Act 2 cleanup process. The affected area appeared to be approximately 30' x 70'; puddled water on the pad in this area showed consistent conductance readings of 1.21-1.28 mS/cm. Two of the rolloffs were still on the pad with the swing gate end raised up on rig mats; while I was on location, a vac truck was used to suck the water out that had collected in the low end of the rolloffs. The north sed trap (.147 mS/cm) and the south sed trap (.441 mS/cm) appeared to be unaffected by the release. The rolloffs were removed and the free water on the pad was vacced while I was on site; a skid steer was scraping the area when I departed. Moody & Associates employees were directing the excavation with conductance meters, and Mike expects confirmation sampling to occur later today or early tomorrow. The site remediation will be referred to the Department's Environmental Cleanups Program. Violations noted.

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 966782

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/26/2022
Comments: On August 26, 2022, the Department conducted an inspection on the Janoscrat 1 well in Derry Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection CEI inspection in response to violations issued under inspection 3400883 where violations were issued due to a possible brine discharge that was discovered on July 29, 2022. The following was observed:The brine tank from where the possible discharge occurred in inspection 3400883 has since been removed, and the area has been mulched and seeded (see photos 1 and 2). The hissing sound and gas odor previously noted on the well head in inspections 3400883 and 3399998 is no longer present (see photo 4). Newly updated operator's information has also been added (see photo 3). Soil conductivity readings were taken on both sides of what once appeared to be the brine puddle. The one taken on the side closest to the well at the former location of the brine tank read, .49 Micro Siemens (see photo 6). The one taken on the side farthest away from the well read .44 Micro Siemens (see photo 7). An additional reading was taken on the side closest to the well at the former brine tank location, but approximately 6 inches of soil was dug before the reading was taken. It read .38 Micro Siemens. A background reading was taken 50 feet west of the well which read .24 Micro Siemens (see photo 9). Overall, the conductivity of the soil at the site of the possible brine release appears to now be comparable to the surrounding soil.Based on observations from today's inspection, the impacted soil appears to have been removed as of August 26, 2022. However, outstanding violations issued during inspection record 3400883 shall remain open since no NOV response or any of the information requested has been received from the operator.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/05/2020
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 896390
Permit API: 125-27157
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Independence Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/07/2020
Comments: On October 5, 2020, I conducted a follow up inspection of the Fred Jones Well Site in Independence Township, Washington County. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported to the Department on 10/4/2020 (CID#352896) . The 10/4/2020 report indicated that approximately 630 gallons of brine was spilled to the well pad. I spoke with Operator representative Casey Barkus on 10/5/2020. Mr. Barkus indicated that a non-structural weld developed a pin hole in the brine tank and caused a stream of brine to shoot across the well pad. Mr. Barkus indicated that the release continued until the brine could be removed from the brine tank. Mr. Barkus indicated that the brine was contained on the well pad and that the pad drain valves were closed. Mr. Barkus indicated that the operator would be utilizing Act 2 clean up as a remediation standard.At the time of inspection, I spoke with operator Josh Boyda. The operator was utilizing third party contractors Miller Environmental and Moody and Associates to guide the remediation of the impacted area. The operator was utilizing a skid steer and excavator to removed impacted material. Mr. Boyda indicated that the impacted material has been placed in the roll off boxes and the crew is awaiting additional disposal boxes to be delivered. I observed 5 rolloff boxes staged within secondary containment and 2 more rolloff boxes located near the impacted area. Mr. Boyda indicated that approximately 12 yards of impacted material has been placed in each rolloff box. The impacted area appeared to be 100' x 60' area located between the brine tank battery and the fenced in well head area. Approximately 6” of material had been removed from the impacted area. Mr. Boyda showed me the non-structural weld on the brine tank that caused the release. The weld in question is located on the brine tank approximately 6' from the bottom of tank on the left side of the brine tank manufacturer information plate.I utilized a Spectrum Field Scout Direct Soil EC meter to screen for conductivity. I screened the impacted area, outlet location and the standing water within the pad drain system.At the impacted area near the fenced well head the meter indicated conductivity of 8.75 mS/cm.At the approximately center of the impacted area of the well pad the meter indicated conductivity of 12.80 mS/cm.At the storm water inlet in the northwest corner of the well pad the meter indicated that conductivity was Or (Or is over range. The meter's max conductivity limit is 20 mS/cm).At the outlet of the pad drain on the meter indicated that conductivity was 0.5 mS/cm.The pad drain outlet appeared to be closed. I recommend that the Operator removed the standing fluid from the outlet and keep the pad drain valve close until remediation is finished and verified.The operator is in compliance with the Department spill policy for reporting and remediation of spills greater than 42 gallons.Violations are being issued for the failure to control a regulated fluid resulting in a release to the ground.The Department requests clarification of how the Operator calculated the amount of fluid released.

Comments: On 9/21/2022, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Chesapeake Hopson well site. It was 67 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. When I arrived on site I met Tim Artman who is overseeing the coil tubing operations and Robert Rueckert who is overseeing the work-over-rig operations.Halliburton finished fracking nine wells on Saturday 8/27/2022 and rigged out on Sunday 8/28/2022. There was a site handoff on 8/29/2022 and the coil tubing and workover rig moved in after that. The two crews are conducting post frac cleanout/drillout operations. The crews were working on the first two wells, the 4HC and 22HC. Tim expects it to take about a week to complete the nine wells.Tim and Robert accompanied me on the inspection. I field tested numerous water/mud puddles around the location with the following results: 4'x20' water puddle near the entrance of the site by two residual waste containers measured 4.12 mS conductance.20'x30' water/mud puddle by brine tanks on south side of pad field tested at 3.79 mS conductance. The brine tanks are left over from fracking operations and not being used by the current operations being conducted on site.I field tested a small 1'x2' puddle of water in the area identified in previous inspections as having high conductance with the current result being 9.33 mS conductance.20'x40' water/mud puddle east of the high conductance area and outside of the secondary containment field tested at 8.61 mS conductance.30'x40' puddle on north edge of pad field tested at 2.32 mS conductance.2'x2' water puddle at the bottom of rock area on east fill slope measured 4.22 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551-025 from this area for laboratory analysis. I contacted Eric Hottenstein concerning the continued high conductance of water/mud on the pad surface and about the elevated conductance water puddle found on the fill slope. He is mobilizing someone to assess the water puddle on the fill slope and reported the following: Chesapeake is pursuing Act 2 for the site in response to inspection 3409693 conducted on 8/11/2022. Chesapeake will begin assessment and cleanup operations when current work activities are concluded and the rig matting and secondary containment plastic has been removed.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed by two retentive grading/infiltration berms. Infiltration berm 2 is not adequately stabilized.The DEP recommends the following:1. Assess the area noted with high conductance water on the fill slope and provide immediate protection as necessary to prevent pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth.2. Continue to remove fluids from the high-conductance areas noted in this and previous inspections.3. Continue to monitor the stabilization of infiltration area 2 and provide additional resources as necessary to achieve at least 70% uniform perennial vegetation.I left the site at 10:30 hrs.

Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/10/2020
Violation Code: 78a54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth and in accordance with 25 Pa. Code §§ 78a.55 – 78a.58 and 78a.60 – 78a.63.
Violation ID: 902030
Permit API: 125-28620
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Robinson Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/10/2020
Comments: This inspection is taking place in response to a spill reported by the operator on 12/10/2020 at approximately 2:15 PM. The operator reported that an open top buster tank overflowed during flow back operations and approximately 20 gallons impacted the ground behind the tank. The operator reported a total of approximately 188 gallons total was spilled, with 168 gallons spilling to secondary containment. The operator is reporting that the spill will be remediated in accordance with 78a.66(c)(1). Nate Smiell and Brandon Carson with Range are on site, on my arrival. The following is observed: The site is currently in flowback operations (Photo 1). The pad drain has been closed. According to Mr. Smiell, he identified the spill at approximately 12:15 PM on 12/10/2020 during a routine inspection of the site. A time for the incident could not be provided at the time of this inspection. Mr. Smiell stated that it could have occurred anywhere between 12 and 24 hours prior to it being found. According to Mr. Smiell the open top tanks are to be inspected and the contents measured every hour. The Department requests these inspection logs be provided for the 24 hours preceding when it was found. Additionally, the Department requests the secondary containment logs for the past month, and at what time was the secondary containment remediated with the vacuum truck? Mr. Carson stated that it was possible that on-site cameras may have recorded the incident. The Department requests more information on this, whether they were able to record the incident and at what time the incident occurred if it was recorded. SPSI is on site and prepping to begin remediation of the site impacted by the spill. The Department requests photographs of the site post clean up as well as the waste manifest once it becomes available. The Department recommended to Mr. Smiell that the operator increase the length of the secondary containment (Photo 2 & 6). Based on this inspection, violations are being noted as immediately corrected. Pending the operator's response, more violations may be forthcoming.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 991493
Permit API: 081-21846
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/13/2023
Comments: On April 13, 2023, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident response to a reported spill at the EQT ARO LLC Chapman Bohlin Pad A. The spill of triethylene glycol and production fluid was reported to DEP by Zac Subra from a failed gasket on a reboiler at one of dehydration units onsite. Mr. Subra estimated about 42 gallons spilled outside of containment onto the well pad surface. DEP met with Mr. Subra and Penn E and R who was overseeing the clean up onsite. EQT contractors were just beginning to excavate the area of impact. The area of impact was about 20 ft. x 15 ft. on the southwest side of the dehydration unit. An additional area of impact under the reboiler was visually stained about 4 ft. x 2 ft. The well pad surface was visually impacted and the area had elevated conductivity in the 2,000 uS/cm range. The area to the southwest of the dehydration unit was scraped about an inch deep to remove the visually impacted soil. The area under the reboiler was excavated about 8 inches deep to remove the visually impacted soil. Conductivity of the finished excavation area according to Penn E and R was 500-1200 uS/cm. EQT was planning on having Penn E and R collect confirmatory samples for the cleanup of the spill.On April 14, 2023, EQT ARO LLC provided the DEP a revision on the estimated amount spilled at the dehydration unit to approximately 15-20 gallons. The estimation was revised based on the amount of soil that was excavated and EQT observation of their midstream system monitoring equipment indicating increased moisture content showing some of the release went into the pipeline. The spilling of triethylene glycol and production fluid outside of containment to the well pad surface is a violation of Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste ManagementAct Section 301. These violations have been immediately corrected.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the JKLM - Headwaters 146 Well Pad located in Ulysses Twp, Potter Co. on 1/10/23 @1045 hours in response to report of a release of 32 gallons of produced fluid from a dehydration unit. The weather was 31 degrees, cloudy, winds WNW @5mph. Activity onsite consists of AES and JKLM personnel bringing Gas Production Equipment back online after the reported release. On 1/9/23 Joe Herrick of JKLM called to report that at 9:45 a.m., a lever control malfunctioned on their 2HU GPU unit and sent a slug of produced water to their dehydration unit resulting in a misting of produced water and a little glycol throughout the exhaust of the dehydration unit. They are estimating about 32 gallons was released. Onsite JKLM personnel estimated the impacted area to be approximately 35' x 25'. Personnel stated before cleanup began elevated conductivity readings of the pad surface were >19.99mS/cm in the immediate vicinity of the dehydration unit and fell to approximately 2-5mS/cm towards the periphery of the impacted area. Onsite Personnel stated the dehydration unit was washed down and fluid was recovered from the secondary containment. Pad material was removed from the impacted area and placed in 2 roll-off containers for disposal. The drains to the perimeter controls remain shut-in and perimeter controls were not impacted. As of today's inspection, the spill area appears to have been backfilled with clean material. Personnel were working onsite to get filters changed in the dehydration unit and get the GPU back online. No areas of elevated conductivity were observed. The spill area appeared adequately remediated.Violations of the following regulations are cited as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED against the 2HU well API#105-21923:CSL 402(b)SWMA 30125 Pa Code 78a.57(a)I departed the site at 1350 hours.

Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions after a truck roll over caused produced fluid to be released along the access road on August 30, 2023. In an email sent to the Department by EQT representative Rick Hall on 9/5/23, he relayed that excavation was complete on the area impacted by the release along the access road. He said that the area of the impact had been delineated by environmental consultant Penn E and R using field instrumentation. He also stated that impacted material which had been excavated was staged within secondary containment on Pad A. Trees have been cleared from the area of the truck rollover on the west side of the access road as well as the area east of the NFG pipeline right-of-way at the north stormwater culvert. The full excavated area has been temporarily stabilized. No fluid was observed in the excavated area. Compost filter sock has been installed as appropriate around the excavated area. No E and S issues noted.On Pad B, nine wells are staged for production. Nine GPUs are present within secondary containment. The electrical conductivity of the fluid in the sump at the east end of the north stormwater channel was 1800 uS/cm. On Pad A, excavated material is tarped and sits within secondary containment. Six wells are staged for production. Six GPUs are present within secondary containment and they appear to be in good condition. Violations remain outstanding for the produced fluid release from the MASS on 12/19/22.

Violation ID: 8274048
Permit API: 051-24570
Unconventional: Yes
County: Fayette
Municipality: Redstone Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/06/2026
Comments: On May 6, 2026, the Department conducted a follow-up inspection to IR 4178322 at the Ritter well site in Redstone Township, Fayette County. Violations were issued in IR 4178322 for failure to conduct long-term maintenance on Post-Construction Stormwater Management Best Management Practices (PCSM BMPs), which appeared to be resulting in accelerated erosion and sedimentation on Tree Farm Road. Tree Farm Road is a township gravel road that connects to the site access road.The Department requested the NOV Response to IR 4178322 from the operator by May 7, 2026. An Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP) for this site was terminated on July 10, 2017.The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of Tree Farm road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in an accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is on site (photo 2). Eight gas wells are onsite that appear to be equipped for production. Well 5H is equipped with a well tag with no observable evidence of a fluid leak to the ground around it (photo 5). The well and operator's information are displayed and visible on this well tag, as required by OGA 3211(g) and OGA 3211(h).The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment appear to be sound at the time of inspection. The GPU units are not equipped with secondary containment. However, the gas wells on site were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. No evidence of a fluid leak, such as staining, was observed on the ground around the GPU units (photos 6 and 7).The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no observable accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 3 and 4). The severe accelerated erosion and sedimentation remains downslope of the well pad on Tree Farm Road (photos 14-24). The Department observed a rock-lined stormwater channel along the access road, which is located upslope of Tree Farm Road. This rock-lined stormwater channel appears to be in need of maintenance, as it appears to be nearly level with the access road (photo 25). Vegetation that appears to be flattened by recent stormwater washout was observed downslope of the rock-lined stormwater channel and at the eastern terminus of the riprap stormwater channel north of the well pad (photos 11-13). The riprap stormwater channel installed north of the well pad is located upslope of the most severely eroded portion of Tree Farm Road. Based on observations from this inspection, violations issued in IR 4178322 shall remain outstanding.

SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/19/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8159311
Permit API: 081-21855
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/19/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that on 9/18/23 a leak was discovered in a GPU on Pad A which led to the release of an unknown quantity of produced fluid to the pad surface. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on Pad A. He showed me where the produced fluid leak occurred inside of GPU #3. He also showed me where the fluid overflowed the interior containment of the GPU and flowed outside of the GPU and onto the pad surface to the southwest of the GPU. A Waste Management crew was excavating the impacted area of the pad during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that the fluid appears to have traveled a couple of inches into the pad surface and then moved toward the southwest pad edge under the surface. A sump present in the stormwater channel along the southwest side of the pad had fluid in it with an electrical conductivity (EC) of 700 uS/cm. Mr. Subra stated that the initial EC reading taken in this sump was approximately 700 uS/cm and later it increased to approximately 1700 uS/cm. A smaller puddle of fluid approximately 25 feet to the north in the channel had an EC of 760 uS/cm during this inspection. No other fluid was observed in the channel or on the pad surface. The Department recommends vacuuming out the fluid in the southwest stormwater channel.Mr. Subra said that they plan to pursue Act 2 remediation due to the unknown volume of the release. Environmental consultant Penn E and R was present during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that Penn E and R were performing electrical conductivity screening and would take samples for the Act 2 remediation. Violations noted for the produced fluid release to the surface of Pad A.
